lemma: Single gate f(x)=[w.x>=t] with integer weights |w_i|<=W, any split S|T with S,T nonempty: rank_F of the cut matrix equals the number of distinct rows over every field F, and that number is at most min(2^|S|, 2W|T|+2). Hence every prefix cut of one gate has rank at most 2Wn+2 under any variable order.
gap: Covers one gate with bounded weights only. Open: (a) multi-gate circuits with one shared variable order (G0003); (b) gates with exponentially large weights, where the bound 2W|T|+2 is useless; the comparator X>=Y (W=2^k) is consistent with it.
proved_step: LEMMA (claimed, self-contained): rows of the cut matrix are nested indicator sets {b: w_T.b >= theta}; choosing b_i in R_i minus R_{i-1} gives a unitriangular submatrix, so rank = distinct rows over every field; distinct rows <= |Sigma_T|+1 <= 2W|T|+2 since subset sums of T lie in [-W|T|, W|T|]. Likely known (OBDD size of small-weight threshold functions, Wegener); not claimed as new.

proved_step: LEMMA (single gate, any field). Let f(x)=[w.x >= t] with integer weights, W = max_i |w_i|, and let [n] = S disjoint-union T with S, T nonempty. Let M be the 2^|S| x 2^|T| cut matrix M[a,b] = f(a,b). Then for every field F, rank_F(M) = number of distinct NONZERO rows of M, and this number is at most min(2^|S|, 2W|T|+2). Proof: row a is the indicator of R_a = {b : w_T.b >= t - w_S.a}; these supports are nested (threshold sets of one linear form). Order the distinct nonzero supports R_1 strictly-in R_2 ... strictly-in R_d and pick b_i in R_i minus R_{i-1} (R_0 empty). Then M[row R_j, col b_i] = [j >= i], unitriangular, so rank >= d; rank <= d is trivial. Bound: w_T.b lies in an integer set of size at most 2W|T|+1; nonempty threshold sets are determined by their least value, so d <= 2W|T|+1 <= 2W|T|+2. The earlier draft said 'rank = number of distinct rows' and omitted the nonzero restriction; that version is false when an all-zero row occurs (example w=(1), t=5, n=2, S={x1}: rank 0, one distinct row).
